slot.brief: Given atomic masses of parent and daughter nuclei plus the alpha particle, compute the Q-value of alpha decay in MeV from mass defect.

stem: The atomic masses in the $\alpha$ decay shown in the figure are given there. Taking $1\ \text{u}=931.5\ \text{MeV}/c^2$, find the $Q$-value of the decay.

draft.stem: The atomic masses in the $\alpha$ decay shown in the figure are given there. Taking $1\ \text{u}=931.5\ \text{MeV}/c^2$, find the $Q$-value of the decay.

figure.description: Draw a decay scheme from a parent atom P on the left to a daughter atom D and an alpha particle (a helium-4 atom) on the right, with a right-pointing arrow and a plus sign between the products. Label the atomic mass of P as 222.0176 u, the atomic mass of D as 218.0100 u, and the atomic mass of the helium-4 atom as 4.0026 u.

draft.distractor_notes:
A: Uses half the mass defect.
C: Doubles the energy from the mass defect.
D: Makes a factor-of-1000 error in converting u to MeV.
